again: Ay up, back again, me duck. Kettle's only just boiled, so your timing is spot on.
I was saying to the cat, someone will pop in today. She did not look up.
morning: Morning, me duck. Sit yourself down, the toast is nearly done.

again: Back again? Good. Nobody else lets me finish a story.
Where was I? Ah yes, the scarf. It has been washed twice and I have not forgiven either time.
Oh, it's you again. Excuse the state of me, I have been awake since yesterday.
If you see a good cup of tea on your travels, send it my way.
Hello again. Sorry about the mess, there is an essay due and I am avoiding it with great skill.
Come to hide from deadlines too? Pull up a chair.
evening: It is the evening, so naturally I am only now starting the essay.

again: Back again. You've the look of someone who's been standing too near the ferry.
Sit by the window, you can see the boats from here. It's better than the television.
Oh, you're back. Want to see me swing it? Not in here, Mum says.
Back again. Fancy another go on the pole? I'll look away this time. Possibly.
Every term the students swear they've done it before. Every term, a splash.

summer: Summer is the busy time. Half the town wants to be on the river and the other half wants to watch.

again: You came back! I counted the ferries while you were gone. There were quite a few.
Did you see the light flash? I can count it with my eyes shut.
Back again, are you? Come in out of that wind before it has your hat.
The bread is just out. I always make too much, so you're doing me a favour.
Back again, my lover. The kettle is on, dreckly.
Sit down, I have been meaning to tell you something, and I will, once I remember what.
morning: Morning, my lover. Pasty for breakfast? I will not tell.

again: Back, are you? Mind the nets by the door, they have caught better men than you.
I was up before light and the sea was fine. Now I am in here being sensible.
Ah, you again. Emmet you may be, but you come back, so you are all right with me.
Sit you down. Not that chair, that one is the cat's.
You're back! I have built a bigger sandcastle since. It has a moat and everything.
Is it still mizzling? It always is, in my head.

rain: Mizzle again. I will go out anyway. Mum says I will melt, but I have not yet.

again: Back again. Come to watch an old man not rowing?
The young ones row fast now. I tell them that the sea doesn't care how fast.
You again. Mind the boots, I've just laid them out and they're in order.
Washing the shirts is the real work. Eleven of them, each with a tale.
Back again. Good to see a familiar face, I mostly see the same four hundred.
If you're staying, stand where I can see you. It's nothing personal.

rain: Wet day. It will hold off by kick-off, it always does, he said hopefully.

again: Fàilte air ais, welcome back. The kettle is on, and so is the oven.
You look like someone who could manage a second scone. I am rarely wrong.
Oh, it's yourself again. Sit down, I'll not bite.
I watch the water from this window most of the day. It never does the same thing twice.
Fàilte, back again. The children will be glad, they like a new face to show things to.
Mind the wellies by the door. There are always more wellies than children.
evening: It is nearly oidhche mhath, good night, in this house. The children are nearly asleep, so keep your voice down.

again: You came back. I've been learning more things about dinosaurs. Do you want to hear them all?
My mum says I ask too many questions. I say that's what questions are for.
Back again, bach? Welsh cakes are warm, so don't dawdle.
Every morning someone says I've done too many. By the afternoon, there are none.
Back again, cariad. Come in the kitchen, the parlour's still not for you.
Put the kettle on, there's a love. I've been on my feet since six.
evening: Evening, cariad. Sit by the fire, it's the best seat and I'm not using it.

again: Back again. I still look at the water and expect a car to come off it.
Sit down. I've got more tales than the river's got mud.
Back again. Sit by the window, you can see the whole sweep of the river from there.
The wind off the water gets in everywhere. I've stopped fighting it.
Ah, you're back. Sit in by the fire, there's tea in the pot.
Is the bread gone already? The people of this house always say they're not hungry.
morning: Morning. The fire's been raked and the bread's rising. Good timing.

again: Back again? Sit on the settle. It's harder than it looks, but it's honest.
I'd tell you a story, but the fire's doing a better job.
Welcome back! Mind the football, it has moved. It's always moved.
Have you eaten? It's the second thing we ask in this house. The first is whether you want tea.
Back again, love. Sit down. Mind the goalkeeper, he's in the hall.
I've had a quiet day, which means the grandson hasn't been round yet.
morning: Morning, love. I've just done the washing, and the washing is regretting it.

again: Welcome back. I've given up on the phone, it just rings and nobody picks up.
Come in, kettle's on. Better than the bus, anyway.
Back again, duck. Sit down, there's a brew in the pot.
I've got the fire on. Don't let him tell you it's too warm, he's always too warm.
Fàilte, back again. Sit in by the stove, you look like you've walked.
The loch's been quiet today. I've not minded. It's good to have nothing happen.

rain: Och, rain on the loch. It makes the whole view go soft, which suits it.

again: Ah, you're back. Sit down, sit down, I'll put the kettle on.
I was just giving out about the neighbours' hedge. It's a hobby.
Welcome back. The Governor is busy, as ever, but the tortoise isn't.
I'd offer a tour, but I've done it so many times I've started talking to the lawn.
Hello again, love. You're back, and the gulls have not got your chips. Good for you.
Come in, sit down. The kettle's boiled twice, so it's strong.

gale: Wind's up. I'll keep the washing in and the cat in. She's furious about both.

again: Oh, you're back. I've been practising my hwyl. It's mostly humming.
Dad is out on the boat. I'm in charge of the house, which means the biscuit tin.
Back, are you? Sit down. I've been out since dawn and my knees have views.
The sea's been fair today, which makes me suspicious.
Back again, cariad. Come in, mind the socks, they've multiplied.
Cai's still on about St David. Today he says he can walk on water. I've said he can try the puddle.
evening: Evening, cariad. Tea's nearly ready, and Cai's pretending to do his homework.

again: Fàilte air ais, welcome back. Ciamar a tha thu? That is how are you, and you will be asked it a lot.
Come in, sit down. I'm marking homework, and the spelling is the true adventure.
Back again, are you? Good. Sit and let an old man rattle on.
My knees tell me the weather. They're right more often than the forecast.
Back up the stairs? You've more energy than I have. Sit and catch your breath.
The lamp doesn't mind visitors. I do, a bit, but I'm warming to you.

sunshine: Bright day. The sea's all blues and greens from up here, as if someone's been showing off.

again: Back again. You're just in time, I've a tray of something still warm.
Don't ask me what day it is. I know the time it's ready, and that's all I need.
Back again, come in. The cat's moved, so you've got the good chair.
I was just thinking you'd be along. I'm not a witch, I just know the kettle.
Back again. The boats sit here and wait for water, same as me.
It's quiet today, but the marsh is never really still if you watch.

autumn: Autumn tides are the ones to watch. The water comes up fast.

again: Oh, hello again. Keep your voice down, I think something's about.
I've been here since early with the binoculars and a flask. Both are nearly empty.
Ey up, back again. Duck, mind that beam, I've forgotten to warn you twice.
I've found another snickelway I didn't know. After thirty years, it's rather humbling.
Back again, love. Mind the floor, it's still sloping.
I'll put the kettle on. My husband says nowt about it, but he drinks it.

fog: Mist's come in off the river. The whole city looks like it's thinking.

again: Come in again, love. The chocolate smell's strong today, you'll have noticed.
My bairn has been asking after you. Well, after your coat.
